label: Most birds lay in spring
claim: The great majority of birds lay their eggs during spring.
quote: The great majority of birds lay during the spring-time.

label: Birds of prey are generally unprolific
claim: Birds of prey with crooked talons generally produce few eggs, except for the kestrel.
quote: All birds of prey, or birds with crooked talons, are unprolific, except the kestrel
scope: Birds of prey, especially the kestrel

label: Healthy fertilized bird eggs have hard shells
claim: A bird egg produced by copulation and laid by a healthy female has a hard shell.
quote: The egg in the case of all birds alike is hard-shelled, if it be the produce of copulation and be laid by a healthy hen

label: Waterbird eggs contain proportionally more yolk
claim: Waterbird eggs contain proportionally more yolk and less white than eggs of land birds.
quote: the eggs of waterbirds have comparatively more of the yellow or yolk and less of the white.
scope: River and marsh birds compared with dry-land birds

label: The blunt end of a bird egg is laid first
claim: The blunt end of a bird egg emerges first during laying.
quote: one end is comparatively sharp, and the other end is comparatively blunt; and it is the latter end that protrudes first at the time of laying.

label: Wind-eggs can form without copulation
claim: Hens and geese can lay unfertilized wind-eggs without ever having copulated.
quote: chickens of the common hen and goose have laid wind-eggs without ever having been subjected to copulation.

label: Chicken incubation is faster in summer
claim: Chicken eggs hatch in about eighteen days in summer but can take as long as twenty-five days in winter.
quote: hens hatch in eighteen days in summer, but occasionally in winter take as many as twenty-five.

label: The heart is the first visible chicken embryo structure
claim: In a chicken egg, the first visible embryonic structure appears after three days and three nights as a beating blood-like heart.
quote: With the common hen after three days and three nights there is the first indication of the embryo

label: Chicken embryos move and chirp around day twenty
claim: At about twenty days of incubation, a chicken embryo moves and chirps when the egg is opened and touched.
quote: About the twentieth day, if you open the egg and touch the chick, it moves inside and chirps

label: Pigeon-kind birds usually lay two eggs
claim: Pigeons, ringdoves, and turtle-doves usually lay two eggs at a time and never more than three.
quote: Birds of the pigeon kind, such as the ringdove and the turtle-dove, lay two eggs at a time; that is to say, they do so as a general rule, and they never lay more than three.

label: Large birds incubate about thirty days
claim: Large birds such as geese and great bustards incubate for about thirty days, while middle-sized birds incubate for about twenty days.
quote: The hatching period is about the same for the larger birds, such as the goose and the great bustard; for the middle-sized birds it extends over about twenty days

label: Cuckoos lay in other birds' nests
claim: The cuckoo builds no nest and lays its eggs in the nests of other birds, sometimes after eating the host's eggs.
quote: The bird eggs, but does not build a nest. Sometimes it lays its eggs in the nest of a smaller bird after first devouring the eggs of this bird

label: Peafowl breeding age and longevity
claim: Peafowl live about twenty-five years and begin breeding around their third year.
quote: Peafowl live for about twenty-five years, breed about the third year

label: Cartilaginous fishes develop from internal eggs
claim: Cartilaginous fishes are first egg-bearing internally and then give birth to live young, except for the fishing-frog.
quote: cartilaginous fishes are first oviparous internally and subsequently viviparous; they rear the embryos internally, the batrachus or fishing-frog being an exception.

label: Smooth shark embryos attach to the womb
claim: Smooth shark embryos develop with a navel-string attached to the womb and are nourished through it after the egg substance is exhausted.
quote: the young develop with the navel-string attached to the womb, so that, as the egg-substance gets used up, the embryo is sustained to all appearance just as in the case of quadrupeds.

label: Cartilaginous fish gestation lasts at most six months
claim: Cartilaginous fishes can conceive an additional brood during pregnancy, and their gestation lasts no more than six months.
quote: Cartilaginous fishes are capable of superfoetation, and their period of gestation is six months at the longest.

label: Cetaceans give birth to live young
claim: All cetaceans with blow-holes rather than gills give birth to live young rather than laying eggs.
quote: The dolphin, the whale, and all the rest of the Cetacea, all, that is to say, that are provided with a blow-hole instead of gills, are viviparous.

label: Dolphins gestate for ten months
claim: The dolphin's gestation period is ten months, and it gives birth only in summer.
quote: Its period of gestation is ten months. It brings forth its young summer, and never at any other season

label: Seals bear and nurse up to three young
claim: The seal gives birth to one or two young, at most three, and nurses them from two teats.
quote: It bears one or two at a time, and three at the most. It has two teats, and suckles its young like a quadruped.

label: Male fish fertilize externally laid eggs
claim: In most egg-laying fishes, only eggs over which the male sheds milt develop into young fish.
quote: only those over which the male sheds the milt or sperm; for when the female has laid her eggs, the male follows and sheds its sperm over them

label: Most oviparous fish spawn annually
claim: Egg-laying fish generally spawn once per year, except the black goby, which spawns twice.
quote: Oviparous fish as a rule spawn only once a year. The little phycis or black goby is an exception, as it spawns twice
scope: Oviparous fishes, especially the black goby

label: Male sheat-fish guard spawn
claim: Male sheat-fish guard the spawning site for forty or fifty days to prevent other small fish from eating the eggs.
quote: the male has to keep watch for forty or fifty days to prevent the-spawn being devoured by such little fishes as chance to come by.

label: Eels arise spontaneously from earth's guts
claim: Eels arise spontaneously from earth's guts that form in mud and wet ground, rather than from mating or eggs.
quote: Eels are derived from the so-called 'earth's guts' that grow spontaneously in mud and in humid ground

label: Most shoaling fishes spawn near the spring equinox
claim: Most shoaling fishes spawn in spring, around the spring equinox.
quote: With shoal fishes parturition takes place in the spring, and indeed, with most fishes, about the time of the spring equinox

label: Cartilaginous fishes are less prolific
claim: Cartilaginous fishes generally produce fewer young than other fishes because they bear live young.
quote: As a rule, cartilaginous fish are less prolific than other fish owing to their being viviparous
scope: Cartilaginous fishes compared with other fishes

label: Domestic swine gestate four months
claim: Domestic swine carry their young for four months and bear no more than twenty piglets in a litter.
quote: Domesticated swine carry their young for four months, and bring forth a litter of twenty at the utmost

label: Sheep and goats gestate five months
claim: Ewes and she-goats carry their young for five months, and well-fed animals in sunny regions can bear twice yearly.
quote: Both ewe and she-goat carry their young for five months; consequently wherever a district is sunny and the animals are used to comfort and well fed, they bear twice in the year.

label: Laconian dogs gestate about sixty days
claim: The Laconian bitch carries her young for about sixty days, and her pups remain blind for twelve days after birth.
quote: The Laconian bitch carries her young the sixth part of a year or sixty days: or more by one, two, or three, or less by one; the pups are blind for twelve days after birth.

label: Cows gestate nine months and usually bear one calf
claim: A cow carries a calf for nine months, gives birth in the tenth month, and usually bears one calf.
quote: The cow goes with calf for nine months, and she calves in the tenth month

label: Mares gestate eleven months and usually bear one foal
claim: A mare carries her foal for eleven months, gives birth in the twelfth month, and usually bears one foal.
quote: The mare carries her foal for eleven months, and casts it in the twelfth.

label: Camels gestate ten months and bear one calf
claim: The camel carries its young for ten months and always bears only one at a time.
quote: The camel carries its young for ten months, and bears but one at a time and never more

label: Newborn elephants can see and walk immediately
claim: A newborn elephant suckles with its mouth rather than its trunk and can see and walk immediately after birth.
quote: The young one, immediately after birth, sucks the mother, not with its trunk but with the mouth; and can walk about and see distinctly the moment it is born.

label: Hinds gestate eight months and usually bear one fawn
claim: Hinds gestate for eight months and usually bear one fawn, though occasionally two.
quote: The period of gestation lasts for eight months. Conception comes on a few days after intercourse; and a number of hinds can be impregnated by a single male. The hind, as a rule, bears but one fawn, although instances have been known of her casting two.

label: Bear cubs are tiny, blind, and undeveloped at birth
claim: Newborn bear cubs are exceptionally small relative to their mother, blind, smooth, and incompletely formed.
quote: Of all animals the newly born cub of the she bear is the smallest in proportion to the size of the mother; that is to say, it is larger than a mouse but smaller than a weasel. It is also smooth and blind, and its legs and most of its organs are as yet inarticulate.

label: Lionesses breed yearly and bear up to six cubs
claim: Lionesses breed once yearly, give birth in spring, generally bear two cubs, and never more than six.
quote: They do not copulate nor bring forth at all seasons indiscriminately, but once in the year only. The lioness brings forth in the spring, generally two cubs at a time, and six at the very most

label: Hares reproduce during pregnancy and while nursing
claim: Hares breed year-round, can conceive another litter while pregnant, and can conceive again immediately after birth while nursing.
quote: They breed and bear at all seasons, superfoetate during pregnancy, and bear young every month.

label: Field mice can devastate crops overnight
claim: Field mice can multiply so rapidly that they consume nearly an entire ripe crop overnight.
quote: sometimes a small farmer will one day observe that it is time for reaping, and on the following morning, when he takes his reapers afield, he finds his entire crop devoured.
